newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-NEAGLE GETS FIRST WIN AS BRAVE, OVER METS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-NEAGLE GETS FIRST WIN AS BRAVE, OVER METS.

text.p: Braves pitcher Denny Neagle tossed a seven-hitter for his first win with his new team and added a key two-run single to lead Atlanta to a 5-2 win over the New York Mets Monday.

Neagle (15-8), acquired from Pittsburgh on August 28, had gone 0-2 with a 6.27 ERA in his first three starts with the Braves. He walked three and struck out three for his second complete game of the season and first victory since August 27.

"I'd be lying to say I wasn't pressing," Neagle said. "I said it wasn't a fluke that I won 14 games with the Pirates. I established my fastball the last few times and I was nit-picking with my changeup."
"We weren't disappointed in his performances before because he was pitching good," Atlanta pitching coach Leo Mazzone said. "I don't care what his record is, he's a heck of a pitcher."

Atlanta, seeking its fifth division title in six years, has won consecutive games following a season-high six-game losing streak and reduced to eight its magic number for clinching the National League East.

New York centre fielder Lance Johnson went 2-for-4 to extend his hitting streak to 15 games. He also got his 20th triple of the season, making him the first National Leaguer to reach 20 triples in a season since Willie Mays in 1957.
Johnson set a Mets' record with his 109th run of the season, surpassing Howard Johnson and Darryl Strawberry.
The Braves scored four runs in the sixth -- the last two on Neagle's single to centre -- to extend their lead to 5-0 and chase starter Pete Harnisch (8-11).
"The hitting is fun, but the important thing is that I gave myself more of a cushion," Neagle said.

Harnisch, who left the game with a contusion of his right hand after Mark Lemke's RBI single hit him on the mound during the Braves' sixth-inning rally, allowed five runs and six hits in 5 2/3 innings to fall to 0-4 in his last seven starts.

In Denver, Ismael Valdes allowed two runs over seven innings to continue his mastery over Colorado and Todd Hollandsworth belted a two-run homer to give the Los Angeles Dodgers their seventh win in eight games, 6-4 over the Rockies.
Valdes (14-7) won his third straight decision, giving up five hits with one walk and six strikeouts. He improved to 3-0 against Colorado this season and 4-0 in his career.

Antonio Osuna pitched a scoreless eighth and Todd Worrell surrendered a two-run homer to pinch-hitter John Vander Wal in the ninth. It was Vander Wal's third pinch-hit homer of the season and ninth of his career.
Los Angeles remained one-half game ahead of San Diego for the top spot in the N.L. West.
The Rockies had their eight-game winning streak snapped. Colorado won eight in a row, a franchise record, on two separate occasions this season.
In San Francisco, Steve Finley led off the 11th inning with a home run off Rod Beck as the San Diego Padres edged the Giants 2-1 to stay right behind the Dodgers in the battle for the N.L. West lead.
San Diego has seven games remaining with Los Angeles.
Finley hit an 0-1 pitch well over the right-field fence for his 25th homer as the Padres won for the seventh time in eight games.
Padres reliever Trevor Hoffman (9-4) allowed one hit, walked two and struck out six in 2 2/3 scoreless innings for the win.
Beck (0-9), who had just 15 career losses before this season, allowed a run and two hits with one walk and three strikeouts over two innings.
The Giants have lost six straight and 11 of their last 12.
San Francisco star Barry Bonds hit his 40th homer of the season in the second inning. It was his 332nd career homer, tying him with his father Bobby for 54th on the all-time list.
